title: Inferring themes
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T17:07:10Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The bank point teaches making a single inference about a character's feelings from clues, at Year 7 and Units 1-2 depth, while the new point needs students to work out a theme about life from patterns across the whole text, which is a different and deeper idea.

draft.title: Inferring themes
card: A theme is an idea about life that a text explores, such as loyalty, power or belonging. It is not the plot and it is not a single word.
A text rarely states its theme. The reader infers it by joining clues into a pattern.
Look at what characters want and how they change, the conflicts they face, and symbols that return, such as a locked gate or a fading photo.
A theme is best written as a short statement, such as 'Loyalty can cost a person their freedom'. Then check that several parts of the text support it.
draft.remember: A theme is an idea about life, inferred from patterns, not a plot summary.

a.q: Which of these is best written as a theme?
opts: Ambition can lead people to betray those they love
A girl moves to a new town and joins a choir
Friendship
The story takes place in winter
a.why: It is an idea about life, written as a full statement that a text could explore. The choir sentence only tells the plot. The single word Friendship names a topic, not an idea about it.
a.clue: A theme says something about life, not just what happens.

b.q: In a story, Tariq keeps failing to leave his village. Each time, a bridge he must cross is broken or flooded. At the end he stays and rebuilds it. Which theme do these patterns best support?
opts: Belonging can matter more than escape
A broken bridge can ruin a journey
Floods are a danger to villages
Travelling always leads to disappointment
b.why: The repeated broken bridge and his choice to rebuild it point to an idea about belonging to a place. The second option only restates an event. The last option goes beyond the clues, which do not show that all travel fails.
b.clue: Join the repeated bridge and his final choice into one idea.

a.best: Ambition can lead people to betray those they love

b.best: Belonging can matter more than escape

problems.detail: The first line gives 'loyalty, power or belonging' as examples of themes, then says a theme 'is not a single word'. This contradicts itself and clashes with question a, where the single word 'Friendship' is wrong. Make these topics that themes are about, not themes.
The right option stands out. It is clearly the longest and the only one that is a full general statement with a qualifier ('can'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

The why refers to 'the second option' and 'the last option', but options appear in random order. In the order shown here, the second option is the correct answer, not the event restatement the why means. Name the options by their words, not their position.

check.summary: Both answers are sound, but the card calls single words like 'loyalty' themes and then says a theme is not a single word. Question a's right option stands out by length and phrasing, and why (b) refers to options by position even though their order is random.

proposal.title: Inferring themes
card: A theme is an idea about life that a text explores. A word such as loyalty, power or belonging names a topic. The theme is what the text suggests about that topic.
A text rarely states its theme. The reader infers it by joining clues into a pattern.
Look at what characters want and how they change, the conflicts they face, and symbols that return, such as a locked gate or a fading photo.
Write a theme as a general statement about people or life, not about one character's events, such as 'Loyalty can cost a person their freedom'. Then check that several parts of the text support it.
proposal.remember: A theme is what a text suggests about a topic, inferred from patterns across the text.

a.q: Which of these is written as a theme?
opts: Ambition can lead people to betray those they love
Mara can only make friends once she joins a choir
The novel's main topics are ambition and family
The story feels tense because it is set in winter
a.why: This is a general statement about what ambition does to people, which a text could explore. The sentence about Mara tells one character's events, which is plot. Naming ambition and family gives topics, not an idea about them.
a.clue: A theme makes a general point about people, not one character.
